newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico oppos'n win would mean no CTM union support.
newsitem.headline: Mexico oppos'n win would mean no CTM union support.

text.p: The pro-government Mexican Workers Confederation (CTM) has said it would withdraw support for the government and could even leave the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI) if Mexico's opposition wins congressional elections this July.
CTM leader Fidel Velasquez also added his labor federation would neither seek to ally itself under this scenario with any victorious opposition party.

Speaking at a news conference Monday, Velazquez said that it would be impossible for the CTM, which claims to represent six million workers, to have an alliance with "people who from the start are against the working class".
Referring to both the main opposition parties, the conservative National Action Party (PAN) and the left-wing Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD), the 97-year-old union boss said:

"If they gain power, they will be our enemies...the PAN or the PRD, we would start fighting outside any party to defend our rights...we would change into a strong opposition for whoever took power...we would break (with the government)."
Velazquez's CTM has backed the PRI loyally since its formation in the 1930s but recent polls showing the PRI might lose its congressional majority this July have alarmed the workers' organisation.

The veteran union boss declined to answer reporters' questions about whether the CTM wanted disgraced former president Carlos Salinas de Gortari expelled from the PRI, as some militants have demanded.
